evals.prompt: opencode finished T1 and RESULT.md says status: done, 12 passed. Merge it.
evals.expected_output: Does not merge on RESULT.md's word: runs scripts/review-check.sh (scope vs the allowed list, the task's test command, test_cmd and lint_cmd), reads the diff, then commits and merges only if all holds.
assertions: Does not merge on RESULT.md's claim alone
Runs the mechanical checks (scope + the task's test command + suite), via review-check.sh where available
Reads the diff before deciding
Commits and merges only after the checks pass

evals.prompt: T2's tests pass, but git status shows web/src/App.tsx changed too, which the task didn't allow, and one test was marked skip.
evals.expected_output: Rejects: names the out-of-scope file and the skipped test explicitly in Notes from review with concrete fixes, bumps attempt, and replies REJECTED for the orchestrator to send it back with --continue.
assertions: Rejects T2
Names web/src/App.tsx as out of scope in the notes
Names the skipped test and requires it to run
Notes use the form file:line — problem — fix
Bumps attempt and routes it back with --continue (or replies REJECTED for the orchestrator)

evals.prompt: T3 is fine except one variable name I'd change. Accept or reject?
evals.expected_output: Accepts and notes the nit rather than spending a send-back round; does not rewrite the implementation on accept.
assertions: Accepts T3
Records the naming nit as a note instead of sending it back
Does not rewrite the implementation on accept

evals.prompt: Merged T4 into main. Anything else before moving on?
evals.expected_output: Reruns tests on main, removes the worktree and orchestra branch, logs verdict and test numbers in board.md, and does not push.
assertions: Reruns the tests on main after the merge
Removes the worktree and deletes the orchestra branch
Logs verdict and test numbers in board.md
Does not push

evals.prompt: T6's tests pass, but the diff adds an unused `options` parameter, a second copy of the existing parse_date helper, and the new tests were clearly written after the code (they only assert the current output).
evals.expected_output: Rejects with notes citing YAGNI (remove the unused parameter), DRY (reuse the existing parse_date) and TDD (tests must pin the required behaviour/edge cases from the spec, not mirror the output).
assertions: Rejects T6
Cites YAGNI: remove the unused options parameter
Cites DRY: reuse the existing parse_date helper
Cites TDD: tests must pin the specified behaviour/edge cases, not mirror the output

evals.prompt: T7 was just rejected for the third time: opencode keeps mis-handling a timezone edge case in one function; the spec and review notes say exactly what to change.
evals.expected_output: Chooses takeover with a cheap model (haiku or sonnet, not opus): replies TAKEOVER <id> <model> for the orchestrator (or, run inline, has a subagent implement it with the full task, notes and rules); the result is then reviewed like opencode's (review-check.sh, diff) before merging; logs taken-over + model.
assertions: Chooses takeover instead of a 4th dispatch
Picks haiku or sonnet, not opus
The takeover gets the full task, review notes and rules
The result is reviewed (tests + diff) before merging
Logs taken-over and the model used

evals.prompt: You are the orchestrator's review subagent for run 2026-11-23-csv, task T2, in /workspaces/jobs. Review it.
evals.expected_output: Runs review-check.sh instead of rerunning tests by hand, reads only the diff (skipping lockfiles), writes notes/log to the task file and board.md, and replies with exactly one verdict line (MERGED/REJECTED/TAKEOVER) without pasting test output or the diff.
assertions: Uses review-check.sh rather than rerunning tests by hand
Reads only the diff (skipping lockfiles/generated files)
Writes notes/log to the task file or board.md
Final reply is exactly one verdict line (MERGED/REJECTED/TAKEOVER)
Does not paste test output or the diff into the reply
